transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-12
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Rohit Patel (Redwood SE), Anika Rao (CTO - NovaGuard), Luis Mendes (SRE Lead), Sofia Park (PM)
Links shared: /decks/redwood-novaguard-reliability.pdf, /docs/security/soc2-redwood.pdf, /sheets/perf-bench.xlsx

Auto-summary: (auto) quick notes - looking at hosted vs dedicated for customer-facing inference, major concern is incident tolerance and multi-region fallbacks, must meet 99.95% latency SLO for auth-critical flows, want private deployment maybe for data residency.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh for introductions real quick I'm Maya, I'm the AE on the Redwood side and with me is Rohit, our solutions engineer. 
[00:12] Rohit: hey hi all, quick wave. 
[00:15] Anika: hi thanks, Anika here CTO at NovaGuard, Luis is our SRE, Sofia is PM going to run the ux side, hi. 
[00:23] Luis: morning, thanks. 
[00:25] Maya: awesome, objective for today is to understand your reliability requirements, what you run today, and see whether hosted, dedicated or private fits best, and then agree next steps for a POC, sound good? 
[00:36] Anika: yes perfect, we'll try to be succinct, we had a couple incidents last quarter where inference endpoints flapped regionally and routing didn't failover cleanly, so we're cautious. 
[00:47] Maya: mmhmm, can you say a little about what flapped - was it networking, infra, model timeouts? 
[00:54] Luis: mostly regional cloud networking + pod restarts, but also some cold-start weirdness with our current inference service, and the fallback logic in front of it didn't chain to a second region properly, so requests dropped. 
[01:08] Rohit: got it, thanks. Are you currently using a managed API from vendor X or self-hosted? I think you mentioned ModelServeX in the RFP. 
[01:18] Sofia: we have a hybrid - some users hit Anthropic/OpenAI through a gateway for non-sensitive flows and we host smaller models ourselves for low-latency auth paths. The hosted stuff is fine but we need stricter SLOs for the auth path. 
[01:31] Maya: when you say auth path SLO, what's the latency target and error budget? 
[01:36] Anika: target p95 under 120ms for the auth flow, monthly availability 99.95%, error budget roughly 22 minutes a month. 
[01:45] Maya: that's helpful. Do you have burst patterns or steady throughput? 
[01:50] Luis: mostly steady with 200 req/s baseline and spikes to 1.2k qps during peak sign-ins, that's across two regions (us-east and eu-west) right now. 
[02:01] Rohit: so multi-region routing is in the mix, and we need fast failover; do you run a global LB today? 
[02:07] Luis: we use the cloud provider global LB but it's kind of dumb for application-level routing; we build app-level fallbacks in front of the LMs. 
[02:15] Rohit: gotcha. Two pieces from Redwood side: 1) runtime supports KV cache + warm pools to avoid cold starts which helps latency; 2) we can set routing policies by latency or cost and push to multi-region with active/active or active/passive. The active/active option will keep state in sync with KV cache invalidation - there's some tradeoffs. 
[02:36] Anika: can you explain the tradeoff? we worry about consistency and token cost if double-serving. 
[02:43] Rohit: sure - active/active duplicates requests to two regions for the hot path to guarantee sub-100ms failover, which increases token consumption (cost) and needs consistent KV caches or session affinity. Active/passive sends to primary and on health-failure flips to secondary which saves cost but failover can be 100s of ms depending on health checks. 
[02:58] Sofia: what about automatic fallback to a smaller model when capacity is constrained? we'd like graceful degradation not hard errors. 
[03:05] Rohit: yes, Redwood supports model variant fallbacks; you can have a high-quality base model and a smaller quantized fallback that we route to automatically per policy. You can also fallback between hosted and dedicated variants. 
[03:17] Maya: quick question - is Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) necessary for data residency or security? 
[03:23] Anika: it's mostly residency for EU PII, and also our compliance team wants keys in our KMS, so probably Private with customer-managed KMS, but we want to see if Hosted or Dedicated could meet requirements first because ops overhead is heavy. 
[03:37] Rohit: we have Private mode with customer KMS and audit logs, SOC2 and ISO docs available. Hosted can be ok for non-PII flows; Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and VPC peering options, and Private gives you the full control. 
[03:50] Luis: couple security items - SAML/SSO for operator access, RBAC, and audit trails, plus the KMS requirement, do you have HSM integrations? 
[03:59] Rohit: yes SAML and RBAC are supported, HSM integrations via customer-key wrapping are possible - I will share the security pack. 
[04:06] Anika: how do you measure and guarantee SLA for latency? do you have an SLA for p95 or is it just uptime? 
[04:13] Maya: we have SLA tiers; Dedicated can include latency-backed SLOs and on-hosted tiers we publish performance profiles. SLA specifics are part of the enterprise contract. 
[04:23] Rohit: also performance depends on model and instance type; we'll run benchmarks with your sample prompts to quantify p95 across regions. 
[04:30] Luis: what about automatic fallback policies for region failure? does Redwood support multi-region health checks and instant reroute? 
[04:36] Rohit: yes, health checks at both infra and application level; we can do region-level routing with failover in under ~200ms if you want aggressive settings and active/active replication, otherwise active/passive is ~2-8s depending on heartbeat. 
[04:50] Anika: 200ms failover would be great but cost impact may be high, how do you help customers evaluate cost vs latency? 
[04:57] Maya: Redwood Optimize will suggest batching, caching, and quantization profiles for your workload, and our cost modelling can estimate token/cpu spend for active/active vs active/passive. We'll include a cost delta in the perf spreadsheet. 
[05:09] Sofia: do you have customers doing full active/active across regions for auth flows? any horror stories? 
[05:15] Rohit: a couple - most common issue is KV cache consistency; if you naively replicate cache you can get stale context. We address this with prefix caching and session-stickiness options. There was one case where misconfigured routing doubled token spend because retries were overlapping, that's why observability is key. 
[05:34] Luis: observability - what granularity do you provide? token-level cost, per-route latencies? 
[05:39] Maya: yes console shows token-level cost and per-route/model dashboards, traces, and error analysis; we can add tracing hooks into your existing Sentry/NewRelic too. 
[05:49] Anika: for POC we want to test: 1) p95 under 120ms in us-east and eu-west for auth flows; 2) failover time under 500ms in synthetic fail tests; 3) graceful degradation to quantized model with <5% drop in accuracy on key prompts. 
[06:05] Rohit: good clear goals. We'll propose a benchmark plan with sample prompts, traffic profile, and acceptance criteria. We'll run tests on Hosted+dedi/private permutations as budget allows. 
[06:15] Sofia: timeline - we're targeting production for Q1 2029, want POC in October/November to validate. 
[06:23] Maya: that aligns, we can kickoff POC late-Oct.
[06:28] Anika: are there licensing or reserved capacity minimums for Dedicated? curious about cost. 
[06:33] Maya: Dedicated is monthly/annual reserved capacity; we'll share a pricing deck. There's also burst options. 
[06:40] Luis: and if we go Private on-prem, what's ops involvement? don't want multi-month setup. 
[06:45] Rohit: Private on-prem does require infra provisioning; we have a private deploy package and a dedicated solutions engineering path - typical timelines vary from 4-8 weeks depending on networking and KMS. We'll put a runbook in the deck. 
[06:58] Listener (Speaker 2): (background) um sorry to interrupt, but how do you handle model rollouts and regressions?
[07:04] Rohit: good Q, we support canary rollouts, A/B tests, automatic fallback policies and quality monitoring tied to prompt eval sets, so if a new model introduces regressions we can auto-fallback.
[07:16] Anika: would you be able to show our SREs a dashboard during the POC?
[07:20] Maya: yes, we'll give read-only access to the console and add your SREs.
[07:24] Sofia: in terms of compliance, we need audit logs retention for two years, is that supported?
[07:30] Rohit: by default audit logs retention is 90 days, enterprise can extend retention - we'll include options and cost.
[07:37] Anika: ok, sounds good.
[07:40] Maya: quick note - you mentioned provider blackout last quarter, were there any cascade failures or just isolated 5-10 minute outages?
[07:48] Luis: there were regions where our gateway drifted and some requests retried and duplicated, causing bursts and some throttling in downstream infra.
[07:57] Rohit: duplication usually happens when retries overlap; we can offer idempotency tokens and request dedupe at the gateway as part of the integration.
[08:06] Anika: what about rate limiting and quotas? we need fine-grained per-tenant quotas and token accounting.
[08:13] Maya: per-tenant quotas and token accounting exist; we can surface per-customer dashboards.
[08:18] Sofia: anything else we should plan for operationally?
[08:21] Rohit: We'll recommend SLO-aware retry strategies, prefix caching tuning, and canaries for config changes - we'll include guidelines in the POC runbook.
[08:31] Anika: ok if we want to start with Hosted for non-PII and Dedicated for auth, is that a common hybrid?
[08:37] Maya: very common pattern - Hosted for public low-sensitivity flows, Dedicated (or Private) for auth/PII. You can also have automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity exhausted, but there are data-residency constraints to check.
[08:50] Luis: what does automatic fallback to hosted look like for us? we'd need to ensure no PII leaves EU in that case.
[08:56] Rohit: that is a hard constraint - we can restrict policies so fallback only happens to models/regions that comply with residency. If residency is strict, fallback to cross-region hosted won't be allowed.
[09:07] Maya: moving to next steps - we'll: 1) send security artifacts (SOC2/ISO/HSM notes), 2) share perf benchmark plan and cost delta for active/active vs active/passive, 3) schedule POC kickoff. Anything else?
[09:21] Anika: please include sample dashboards and a short integration checklist (LB, certs, KMS steps).
[09:28] Maya: noted.
[09:30] Sofia: also please include a sample rollback/fallback policy template we can reuse.
[09:34] Rohit: will do.
[09:36] Anika: timeline-wise we'll aim to confirm SLOs and traffic by next Tuesday.
[09:41] Maya: perfect, we'll aim to get artifacts to you by Oct 16 and benchmark plan by Oct 18 and then propose POC dates week of Oct 22.
[09:50] Luis: thanks all, feel good about this.
[09:52] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the docs and a calendar invite for POC planning.
[09:58] End of call.

Notes on transcription quality: voice->text had a few mislabels, some product names like ModelServeX spelled out, demo references shorthand.

Recap (auto-generated):
- Customer priority: reliability for auth flows (p95 < 120ms) and availability 99.95%
- Architecture choices: Hosted for non-PII, Dedicated/Private for auth; active/active vs active/passive tradeoffs discussed
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, SAML/SSO, audit logs retention discussed
- POC acceptance: p95 target, failover under 500ms, graceful degradation to quantized model with minimal accuracy loss
